title: What continuing education do nurses need to renew a Florida license?
description: Florida Board of Nursing renewal CE as at November 2026: 24 hours per biennium, mandatory medical errors, laws, impairment, trafficking and domestic violence.
shortAnswer: Florida registered nurses and licensed practical nurses must earn one contact hour of continuing education for each month of the licensure cycle, which is 24 hours per two year biennium, and report it to the Florida Department of Health's CE Broker tracking system before renewing. The Florida Board of Nursing requires mandatory courses within those hours: prevention of medical errors, Florida laws and rules, and human trafficking every biennium, recognizing impairment every other biennium, and domestic violence every third biennium.
keyTakeaways: Section 464.013(3), Florida Statutes, lets the Board of Nursing prescribe up to 30 hours biennially; Rule 64B9-5.002 sets one contact hour per calendar month of the cycle.
Every biennium: 2 hours of prevention of medical errors, 2 hours of Florida laws and rules, and 2 hours of human trafficking. Every other biennium: 2 hours of recognizing impairment in the workplace.

Domestic violence is required every third biennium and HIV/AIDS once before the first renewal. The board's website and the rule describe the domestic violence hours differently, which nurses should check.
Nurses certified by an NCCA or ABSNC accredited specialty program are exempt from general CE, but not from the 2 hour human trafficking course.
Advanced practice registered nurses must complete 3 hours on safe and effective prescribing of controlled substances within the biennial hours.
regulator: Florida Board of Nursing, Florida Department of Health
appliesTo: Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses with a Florida license
Advanced practice registered nurses licensed under section 464.012, Florida Statutes
Hospitals, nursing homes, home health agencies and staffing firms employing Florida licensed nurses
Not nurses practicing in Florida on a multistate license issued by another Nurse Licensure Compact state

sections.heading: How many CE hours do Florida nurses need?

blocks.text: Florida nurses need one contact hour for each calendar month of the licensure cycle, which is 24 hours for a full two year biennium. [Rule 64B9-5.002(1)](https://www.flrules.org/gateway/ruleNo.asp?id=64B9-5.002), Florida Administrative Code, states: "During each biennium, one contact hour must be earned for each calendar month of the licensure cycle."

The statutory ceiling is in [section 464.013(3), Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0464/Sections/0464.013.html), which says the board "shall by rule prescribe up to 30 hours of continuing education biennially as a condition for renewal." As at November 2026 the board's rule uses 24 of those 30 hours.

The board's [registered nurse renewal page](https://floridasnursing.gov/registered-nurse-renewal/) shows how the 24 hours divide in a typical cycle: 16 general hours approved by a state or national organization authorized to accredit nursing continuing education, plus the mandatory subject courses. All courses can be live or home study.

sections.heading: Which courses are mandatory for Florida nurses, and how often?

blocks.text: Rule 64B9-5.002(2) makes six courses a mandatory part of the hours, each on its own schedule. The board's website adds that all mandatory courses must come from a Florida Board of Nursing approved provider, except the human trafficking course.

blocks.title: Point to check: domestic violence hours
blocks.text: Rule 64B9-5.002(2) lists the domestic violence course as "a mandatory part of the hours required in subsection (1)." The board's renewal page states that domestic violence is "in addition to the 24 hours required for renewal." Until the board reconciles the two, nurses in a domestic violence biennium can avoid any shortfall by completing the 2 hours on top of 24.

The human trafficking content is fixed in statute. Section 464.013(3)(c) requires a 2 hour course covering the types and extent of human trafficking, risk factors, social services, the hotlines of the National Human Trafficking Resource Center and the US Department of Homeland Security, validated assessment tools and indicators, procedures for sharing information with a patient, and referral options. It is compared with other states in [human trafficking training requirements for healthcare](/regulations/human-trafficking-training-requirements-healthcare).

sections.heading: What do newly licensed Florida nurses need at their first renewal?

blocks.text: Nurses licensed by examination during the current biennium are exempt from the general hours, but must still complete the mandatory courses. The board lists them as 2 hours of medical errors, 2 hours of Florida laws and rules, 2 hours of recognizing impairment in the workplace, 2 hours of human trafficking and 1 hour of HIV/AIDS.

Rule 64B9-5.002(3) treats endorsement differently. A nurse who endorses into Florida, or whose license is reactivated or reinstated during a biennium, must accrue one contact hour for each calendar month remaining in the biennium, with no hours required if six months or less remain. The exemption applies only if the license is renewed on time.

sections.heading: Which Florida nurses are exempt from continuing education?

blocks.text: A nurse certified by a health care specialty program accredited by the National Commission for Certifying Agencies (NCCA) or the Accreditation Board for Specialty Nursing Certification (ABSNC) is exempt under section 464.013(3)(a). The certification must be reported to CE Broker. The exemption does not cover the human trafficking course, because section 464.013(3)(c) applies "notwithstanding the exemption."

Rule 64B9-5.002(5) exempts a nurse who is the spouse of a member of the Armed Forces and was absent from Florida because of the spouse's duties, with proof. A nurse practicing in Florida on a multistate license issued by another Nurse Licensure Compact state follows the CE rules of the issuing state, not Florida's, according to the board.

sections.heading: What extra CE do Florida APRNs need?

blocks.text: Advanced practice registered nurses must complete at least 3 hours on the safe and effective prescription of controlled substances as part of the biennial hours, under section 464.013(3)(b). The course must be offered by a statewide professional association of physicians accredited for AMA PRA Category 1 credit, the American Nurses Credentialing Center, the American Association of Nurse Anesthetists or the American Association of Nurse Practitioners, and may be delivered by distance learning.

Rule 64B9-5.002(4) lets an RN who also holds a current APRN license satisfy both licenses with RN continuing education, or meet up to 50% of the requirement with continuing medical education. APRNs who hold a DEA registration also carry the federal one-time 8 hour training in [the DEA MATE Act requirement](/regulations/dea-mate-act-training-requirement).

sections.heading: How do Florida nurses report CE and when do licenses expire?

blocks.text: Nurses report completed hours to the Department of Health's tracking system, CE Broker, before renewing, and do not send certificates to the board. The department renews a license on receipt of completed CE reported in CE Broker, the renewal application and fees.

RN licenses renew in three groups. The board lists current expirations at midnight Eastern Standard Time on April 30, 2027 for Group 3, April 30, 2028 for Group 1, and July 31, 2028 for Group 2. A nurse renewing a delinquent license must report CE for the current and the previous cycle.

sections.heading: How can a Florida employer map nursing CE to evidence?

blocks.text: Because the mandatory courses run on one, two and three biennium cycles, employers benefit from tracking each nurse's position in the cycle rather than a single hours total. sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each Florida course as its own obligation with its own cycle, so the impairment and domestic violence courses surface in the right biennium instead of every renewal. Where a rule and regulator guidance differ, as with domestic violence hours, the discrepancy is recorded against both sources for review. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Do Florida nurses need the human trafficking course every renewal?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 464.013(3)(c) requires every licensee to complete a 2 hour human trafficking course for every biennial renewal on or after January 1, 2019. It applies even to nurses who are otherwise exempt through specialty certification, and the course does not have to be approved by the Board of Nursing if it meets the statutory content.

faqs.q: Do I need to send CE certificates to the Florida Board of Nursing?
faqs.a: No. The board instructs nurses not to submit certificates and to report credits to the Department of Health's tracking system at CE Broker. Completed hours must be reported there before renewal.

faqs.q: Can Florida nurses take all their CE online?
faqs.a: The Board of Nursing's renewal page states that all courses can be live or home study. Mandatory courses other than human trafficking must still come from a board approved provider listed in CE Broker.

faqs.q: Does a nurse with a multistate compact license from another state need Florida CE?
faqs.a: No. The board states that nurses practicing in Florida under the privilege of a different party state license are not required to pay Florida fees or complete Florida continuing education. They follow the requirements of the state that issued the license.
